executive_readout: Linear says it is receiving more enterprise customer security reviews and wants the process to run more smoothly. Public evidence already answers many baseline questions: Linear documents SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA/BAA support, a Trust Center, Enterprise SAML/SCIM, audit logs, access restrictions and data-residency options. That makes generic certification or identity-control discovery low-value. The useful first-call work is to locate where reviews still create manual effort despite that assurance stack, then define what “smoother” should change operationally. Public evidence can suppress redundant questions, but it cannot tell us whether the remaining friction is questionnaires, evidence access, technical escalations or something else.

premium_brief_markdown:
Linear’s public material removes a large amount of low-value first-call discovery. It already documents SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and HIPAA/BAA support [E1], operates a Trust Center with standard assurance material [E2], supports Enterprise SAML and SCIM [E3], and documents audit logs plus access and data-residency controls [E4][E5]. The booking therefore should not trigger a generic “tell me about your security program” conversation. The useful problem is where enterprise customer security reviews still create manual effort despite that existing evidence stack.

The first question should locate the residual friction precisely: recurring questionnaires, evidence access, bespoke technical/control questions, customer security calls, or another part of the review workflow [U1]. That framing matters because each answer points to a different operational problem. Rewriting the same questionnaires suggests reuse and response-system friction. Repeated security/engineering participation suggests an expert-interruption bottleneck. Customers asking for material not covered by the Trust Center suggests a recurring evidence gap. None of those should be assumed before the prospect says so [R1].

The second question should define what “smoother” means operationally [U2]. Faster standard responses, reusable evidence, fewer security-team interruptions, hands-on support for complex reviews and a broader governance fix are not interchangeable outcomes. The consultant should leave the call knowing which change matters and only then map it to a service [R2]. Enterprise Sales Security Enablement becomes relevant if the prospect confirms recurring questionnaire, evidence or customer-review workflow friction. Advisory vCISO becomes relevant only if reviews repeatedly expose broader control or governance work that sits beyond the review process itself.

Avoid asking whether Linear has SOC 2, ISO, SAML, SCIM or audit logs; those facts are already available publicly. Do not assume the Trust Center is failing because review volume is rising. Do not introduce budget, procurement, stakeholder mapping or a deadline just because those are common sales questions; the booking does not expose those dimensions and consultant policy does not require them. The consultant’s advantage here is restraint: demonstrate that the obvious assurance baseline is already understood, spend the conversation on the two unresolved operating questions, and let the prospect’s answers earn any deeper branch.
